title: Memory Echo in Single-Agent Long-Term Memory: Lifecycle Evaluation and Provenance-Guided Mitigation
abstract: arXiv:2610.17763v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Long-term memory supports agents across sessions. Repeated retrieval and write-back can let one historical claim occupy multiple retrieval positions and influence current answers without independent evidence. Existing work examines retrieval, updating, and question answering, leaving same-source record accumulation and post-correction persistence underexplored. Motivated by research in social cognition and memory psychology on repeated exposure, retrieval, and revision, we define \emph{Memory Echo} as the excess retrieval exposure gained by historical information from the same source without additional independent evidence, and introduce MEchoBench to evaluate its emergence, correction resistance, persistence, and effect on answers. To address this phenomenon, we introduce the Family--Provenance--Authority framework (FPA). translated_title: 单智能体长期记忆中的“记忆回声”：生命周期评估与来源引导的缓解方法
translated_abstract: 长期记忆为智能体提供跨会话的支持。重复的检索与写回操作可能使一条历史性声明占据多个检索位置，并在缺乏独立证据的情况下影响当前答案。现有工作主要研究检索、更新和问答，而对同源记录累积以及纠正后持久性问题的探索仍不足。受社会认知与记忆心理学中关于重复曝光、检索和修正的研究启发，我们将“记忆回声”定义为：同一来源的历史信息在没有额外独立证据的情况下获得的过量检索曝光，并引入 MEchoBench 基准来评估该现象的产生、纠正抗性、持久性及其对答案的影响。为应对这一现象，我们提出了家族-来源-权威框架（Family--Provenance--Authority，FPA）。具体而言，FPA 为每个来源家族选取一个代表性记录，并对旧记录参与后续分析的资格进行约束……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文定义了单智能体长期记忆中的“记忆回声”现象——即同源历史信息无需独立证据即可通过重复检索与写回获得过量曝光并影响当前答案，并提出 MEchoBench 基准和家族-来源-权威（FPA）框架来评估与缓解该问题。
en_tdlr: This paper defines "Memory Echo," where same-source historical information gains excess retrieval exposure without independent evidence through repeated retrieval and write-back, and introduces MEchoBench along with the Family--Provenance--Authority (FPA) framework to evaluate and mitigate this phenomenon.
